protocol.description:
This protocol allows a client to query and configure displays managed by the NVIDIA Display Config Server (DCS).
Warning: This protocol is unstable and subject to change without notice.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_manager
interface.description: This object is where the usage begins. The configuration tool will connect to the wayland socket and create a new manager object. This manager object is used to get the DCS companion object to a given wl_output advertised by the system. It is also used to create topology objects which are used for atomically updating the system state.

request.name: get_output

description.summary: create a zwp_dcs_output for a wl_output

request.description: Creates a zwp_dcs_output object which extends the provided wl_output.

request.name: create_topology
request.description: Creates a zwp_dcs_topology object which is used to atomically commit configuration changes across multiple displays.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the manager object. Objects created through it, such as zwp_dcs_output and zwp_dcs_topology, are not affected and remain valid.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_output
interface.description:
This object is used to describe the current physical display count and layout. It extends wl_output, meaning wayland global objects visible in wl_registry will be added and removed to reflect the current display state. Most of the display information comes from wl_output, however this allows us to attach display config server specific information to each output.
Note that the events here will be resent on any changes. Unlike wl_output's values which are sent once, these may be resent if there have been any changes.

event.name: mode
event.description:
Sends one supported mode for this output. The id is an opaque value chosen by the server that identifies this mode on this output for the lifetime of the zwp_dcs_output. Clients pass it back to zwp_dcs_display_configuration.set_mode and match it against current_mode and preferred_mode. Ids carry no other meaning: they need not be contiguous, ordered, or comparable across outputs.
All mode events for an output are sent before current_mode, preferred_mode, and done.

event.name: current_mode
event.description: Identifies the mode currently set on this output, by the id given in a previous mode event. Sent after the mode list; may be resent on its own when the active mode changes.

event.name: preferred_mode
event.description: Identifies the display's preferred mode, by the id given in a previous mode event. Sent after the mode list.

event.name: device

description.summary: the DRM device for this output

event.description: The DRM device that drives this output. The array holds the dev_t of the device's primary node as an array of sizeof(dev_t) bytes in native byte order, the same encoding wp_linux_dmabuf_feedback uses for main_device. Clients compare devices by value rather than by node path, and must not assume a particular size for dev_t.

event.name: number
event.description: The ID number (1-n) of the display.

event.name: done

description.summary: all DCS output state has been sent

event.description: Signals that all DCS output state has finished sending.

request.name: create_configuration
request.description: Create a new zwp_dcs_display_configuration object for this output.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this object. The underlying wl_output and any zwp_dcs_display_configuration objects created from this output are not affected.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_display_configuration
interface.description:
This object allows for configuring one display in the system. It takes care of updating only one display and will be part of a broader topology update which will control setting multiple configurations across multiple displays/devices. Think of this like a description of display state which will be applied during an atomic topology commit.
The configuration only needs to include the pieces of state which need to be changed. Values which are omitted will not have their state changed from what the display is currently using.

entry.name: invalid_state
entry.summary: a component of this double-buffered commit could not be applied

request.name: set_mode
request.description: Records the mode to set with this configuration update, identified by the id from a zwp_dcs_output.mode event of the output this configuration was created from. An id that does not belong to that output causes the topology commit to fail with an error event on this configuration.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: id of the mode to set

event.name: error
event.description: Error returned on this object if part of its configuration failed.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this configuration and discards its pending state. If it has been added to a topology, it is removed from that topology and takes no part in later commits of it. Sub-protocol configuration objects created for this configuration are not destroyed, but the state staged on them can no longer be applied and the client should destroy them as well.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_topology
interface.description: A topology combines multiple zwp_dcs_display_configuration objects into one atomic state commit. These configs represent changes to an individual display and the topology represents changes to the entire display wall. The topology has a set of configs added to it, then once everything is specified the topology is committed. If there are any issues with the attempted configuration change then the topology will return an error event signaling failure, and the specific display_configuration objects causing the problem will receive error events to hint what caused the commit to be rejected.

entry.name: failed
entry.summary: a component of this double-buffered commit could not be applied; the configuration objects will have an error posted to disclose more

entry.name: duplicate_configs
entry.summary: multiple configurations were added that reference the same output object

request.name: add_configuration

description.summary: add a configuration to the topology

request.description: Adds a configuration to the topology to be committed.

request.name: commit
request.description:
Commits the changes to all configurations. The server answers every commit with exactly one of the done or error events, sent after any zwp_dcs_display_configuration.error events that belong to the same commit. Commits are processed in order, so a client that waits for the reply before committing again can match each reply to its request.
If the commit fails and error is sent, nothing was applied and the topology stays alive with all of its pending state. The client can adjust the offending configuration and commit again without rebuilding the topology.
If the commit succeeds and done is sent, the commit is complete and the topology's lifetime is over. The client must destroy it, along with any sub-protocol topology objects created from it. The configurations that were added to it have been applied and should be destroyed as well. The only request permitted on these objects after done is destroy.

event.name: done
event.description: Sent when every configuration in the committed topology was validated and applied. The displays are now in the requested state and the topology is finished, see commit for what the client must do next.

event.name: error
event.description: Sent when the commit was rejected. Nothing was applied and the topology stays alive so the client can correct it and commit again. The configuration objects that caused the rejection receive their own error events before this one.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this topology. Any uncommitted state is discarded. This is the required final request after a commit reports done, and may also be sent at any other time to abandon the topology. The zwp_dcs_display_configuration objects added to it are not destroyed and may be added to another topology. Sub-protocol topology objects created from this topology are not destroyed, but since they can only be applied through this topology's commit the client should destroy them as well.
